title: Traveling this Thanksgiving? Duke Energy Florida shares 4 tips to save energy while away
summary: With 81.5 million Americans projected to travel at least 50 miles from home for Thanksgiving celebrations this year, Duke Energy Florida is sharing four tips to help customers save energy while they’re away.
body_markdown:
ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. – With[4.6 million](https://newsroom.acg.aaa.com/46-million-floridians-expected-to-travel-for-thanksgiving/) Floridians projected to travel at least 50 miles from home for Thanksgiving celebrations this year, Duke Energy Florida is sharing four tips to help customers save energy while they’re away.


**Pre-travel checklist:**


- **Adjust the thermostat.** Use a programmable thermostat’s “vacation” mode or manually adjust the temperature a few degrees lower or higher, depending on the forecast, before you leave. Simply adjusting the thermostat between 7 °F and 10 °F from its normal setting for eight hours a day can save up to[10%](https://web.archive.org/web/20260603001100/https:/www.energy.gov/energysaver/programmable-thermostats) in annual heating and cooling costs.


- **Adjust the water heater.** Water heating can account for[14% to 25%](https://stage.energy.gov/cmei/femp/home-energy-checklist) of the energy used in a home. If your water heater has a “vacation” or energy-saving mode, consider using it while you’re away. Follow the manufacturer’s instructions before turning off or changing the settings on any water heater.


- **Unplug unused electronics.** TVs, game consoles, coffee makers, rechargeable toothbrushes and more can still use energy when they are turned off, idle or in “standby” mode, often making up between[5% and 10%](https://standby.lbl.gov/frequently-asked-questions) of a home’s total energy use.


- **Turn off lights and fans.** If you keep lights on for security, place them on timers and switch to LED bulbs, which use up to[80%](https://stage.energy.gov/articles/5-tips-energy-saving-renters) less energy than traditional incandescent bulbs.


**Our view:**


“We encourage our customers who are traveling during the holidays to take a few minutes to walk through their homes before hitting the road,” said Melissa Seixas, Duke Energy Florida state president. “These quick, simple adjustments can go a long way toward helping them save energy and money while they’re away.”


For more tips to manage energy use, as well as information about Duke Energy Florida's energy efficiency programs, please visit[duke-energy.com/Savings](https://www.duke-energy.com/home/products) .
